proof:
Since $A_t\subseteq A$, the deformed family still obeys midpoint compatibility. The three lifted bodies are the exact integer fibers of their convex hull: at base $0$ every mixture uses equal total weights on the two endpoints, so its continuous point lies in $K$ by convexity and midpoint compatibility. At the endpoint bases a mixture uses only its own fiber.

For variable $\xi$ near $y$, the three cap masses are
$$
F_i(\xi,t)=|K\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge v_i\cdot\xi\}|
           +|A_t\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge 2v_i\cdot\xi-h_i\}|.
$$
The traces on $B$ remain supported at $h_i$ and contribute zero area. The $K$ and pulled-back $A$ thresholds remain proper near $(y,0)$. Parallel section lengths are continuous at proper cuts by concavity. Fubini and the exact homothetic pullback, with threshold $(2v_i\cdot\xi-h_i-tv_i\cdot p)/(1-t)$, make the functions $C^1$ on a neighborhood of $(y,0)$ and give $\nabla_\xi F_i(y,0)=-s_i v_i$ and $\partial_t F_i(y,0)=-L_i(p)$. The derivative of $(F_i(\xi,t)-q)_{i=1}^3$ in $(\xi,q)$ is nonsingular. Indeed, a kernel vector $(\dot \xi,\dot q)$ satisfies $-s_i v_i\cdot\dot \xi-\dot q=0$ for all $i$. Multiplying by $\lambda_i$ and summing gives $\dot q=0$, and spanning gives $\dot \xi=0$. The implicit function theorem gives $y(t),q(t)$. Differentiating $F_i(y(t),t)=q(t)$ and taking the same weighted sum gives $q'(0)=-\overline L(p)$.

The middle trace margins sum to zero, so the caps cover the whole middle plane and bound each middle point's depth by $q(t)$. At either endpoint the mixed point depth equals ordinary point depth on that fiber: every containing ambient cap pays at least the ordinary depth there, and any prescribed ordinary endpoint cap extends to an ambient cap missing both other compact fibers by a finite integer tilt toward the endpoint. The ordinary endpoint maxima become $(1-t)^2m_A$ and $m_B$ under this contraction. Strict original gaps and continuity of $q(t)$ keep both below $q(t)$ for small $t$. Since $M'(0)=-2a$, the quotient derivative is as stated. When it is negative the certificate drops below the original normalized maximum.

For the last assertion, choose any interior point of $B$. Each $h_i$ strictly exceeds the corresponding normal evaluated there, so $\sum_i b_i=-\sum_i h_i<0$. The three $A$ traces cover the plane, since missing all three would imply $0<\sum_i b_i<0$. With null singleton-capture regions they capture almost every point of $A$ at least twice. The actual chord-weight theorem applies to exactly these $A,K,B,y,v_i$, giving $\max_i\lambda_i\le3\Lambda/4$. Thus the load is at least $\Lambda-\max_i\lambda_i\ge\Lambda/4$. The weighted shell lemma with $d=2$ and weights $\lambda_i$ gives $\overline L(p)\ge a/2$. Substitution proves the final derivative bounds.

statement:
Let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^2$ be convex bodies at the only integer bases $-1,0,1$, with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Fix $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and nonzero spanning normals $v_i$ for $1\le i\le3$ with $\sum_i v_i=0$. Put $h_i=h_B(v_i)$ and $b_i=2v_i\cdot y-h_i$. Suppose the caps $v_i\cdot(x-y)+(v_i\cdot y-h_i)z\ge0$ have common raw mass $Q$ and proper $A,K$ cuts. Write $a=|A|$, $M=|A|+|K|+|B|$, $U_i=|A\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}|$, and $a_i,k_i$ for the $A,K$ chord lengths divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$. Put $s_i=2a_i+k_i$, $\lambda_i=1/s_i$, $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$, and
$$
L_i(p)=2U_i+(b_i-v_i\cdot p)a_i,\qquad
\overline L(p)=\frac{\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)}{\Lambda}.
$$

For every $p\in A$, contract $A$ to $A_t=p+(1-t)(A-p)$ and keep $K,B$ fixed. For all sufficiently small $t\ge0$ there is a $C^1$ meeting point $y(t)$ with $y(0)=y$ and a common cap budget $q(t)$ with $q(0)=Q$, obtained by substituting $y(t)$ for $y$ in the same three ambient caps. They cover the full middle plane, and $q'(0)=-\overline L(p)$. If $Q$ is the original global raw maximum and the two ordinary endpoint maxima are strictly below $Q$, the new global raw maximum is at most $q(t)$ for all sufficiently small $t\ge0$. Writing $M(t)=|A_t|+|K|+|B|$,
$$
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\frac{q(t)}{M(t)}\right|_{t=0}
=\frac{-M\overline L(p)+2aQ}{M^2}.
$$
In particular the optimized normalized depth strictly decreases if $\overline L(p)>2aQ/M$.

If the three original caps attain the true depth at $(0,y)$ and every singleton-capture region of the $A$ traces is null, then $\overline L(p)\ge a/2$ for every $p\in A$. The derivative above is then at most $(-Ma/2+2aQ)/M^2$. At a budget ratio $Q/M<2/9$ this last expression is less than $-a/(18M)$.
